title: The mini-guest unit tests stall while a real campaign runs on the same host
foundBy: session agent, running `make ci` while two live campaigns ran on the same host

evidence.verified: With two campaigns live on the host, `TestCampaignDoctorPassesAMemberOnTheShippedHarness` took 121 seconds before the fix and 1.4 after. The `internal/cli` package took 21 seconds, where it had passed the 10-minute timeout. `make ci` then passed, with all 9 smoke scenarios replayed, before a rebase onto 02c755f that changed only ci.yml.

resolution: The mini guest now carries its own `pgrep`, which sees no process, as a real member's sees only its own machine. The member probe run on the host no longer counts another campaign's turn drivers.
details:
The mini-guest tests in `internal/cli` stand a directory on the host in for a member, and their fake `cs-sandbox` runs each command there on the host. The member probe counts running turn drivers with `pgrep -fa 'cs-[c]laude-turn '`. On the host, that also counts the turn drivers of any real campaign running there.

With two campaigns live, `openMissionWhenQuiet` saw their orchestrators as the test's own, busy in a turn. It waited out its two-minute bound in every test that runs `create`. `TestCampaignDoctorPassesAMemberOnTheShippedHarness` took 121 seconds instead of a few, and the `internal/cli` package passed the 10-minute test timeout, so `make ci` failed. A unit test should not depend on what else the host is running.
